answer: A farm that wants 169 keys therefore pays 169 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the summit seed, the lagoon timing is verifiable from the dawn record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 346 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
